gddGap: The menu design doc shows a poster 'Rust Notice 114 / CURFEW' but the main GDD never says the Rust issue curfews or numbered notices (canon open question 1). Kept as flavour pending owner approval.
name: Rust Notice 114
summary: A cold, official curfew notice the Rust post on walls, always crossed out by the neighbourhood.
body: Brick red and bossy, it is the Rust's way of speaking to the block. Somebody always gets to it first with a hand-inked cross-out.

gddGap: The menu poster 'Local Heroes Benefit: Keep the Lights On' implies community fundraising events, which the GDD does not describe.
name: Local Heroes Benefit
summary: A neighbourhood benefit night, Keep the Lights On, that keeps the community together under the Rust.
body: Posters for it turn up on the walls the Rust have not yet cleaned. It is proof the block is still looking out for each other.

gddGap: The GDD says 'urban districts' but names none. Built from the mustard-yellow storefronts and corner shops of the Theme.
name: Mustard Row
summary: The shopfront street of mustard-yellow corner shops, where the first arena could sit.
body: Awnings, hand-lettered signs and shutters the Rust have chained down. Reopening a shop here is the first small win.

gddGap: No districts are named in the GDD. Built from the forest-green basketball courts of Zed's block.
name: Greenline Courts
summary: The forest-green court district, shut down and waiting for kids to come back.
body: Chain-link, faded lines and a hoop with no net. When the Rust are pushed back, the first sound should be a bouncing ball.

gddGap: No districts are named in the GDD. Built from the food stalls and community gardens of the Theme and Zed's mother's stall.
name: Stewpot Gardens
summary: Food stalls and fenced-off community gardens, the warmest corner of the city.
body: Stall awnings, planters behind Rust fencing and the memory of stew. Reclaiming it means the smell of dinner is back.

gddGap: No districts are named in the GDD. Built from the open windows with music and the murals celebrating local heroes.
name: Songwindow Heights
summary: Tall apartment blocks where music used to drift from open windows, now watched by Rust towers.
body: Mural walls rise between the buildings, mostly painted over. It is the district where the music comes back.
